type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 270409 RECIPIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS, 252400 UNKNOWN_BANK_CODE, 251400 INVALID_ACCOUNT.

gotchas: Auth (OAuth2 client credentials): POST grant_type=client_credentials, client_id and client_secret as application/x-www-form-urlencoded to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token (same token URL for sandbox and production), then send `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Docs (Authentication): "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. FLUTTERWAVE_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS = base64(client_id:client_secret) is an afrotools convention, decoded locally; Flutterwave never receives it. Sandbox base URL: https://developersandbox-api.flutterwave.com ("We archive your test data after 30 days.")

Headers: send X-Idempotency-Key on this POST. Docs (Idempotency): "For all `POST` endpoints, include an idempotency key in the request header (`X-Idempotency-Key`)." The API reference marks it optional; the headers guide lists it under 'Mandatory API Headers'. A reused key replays the first response ("the response will include the header `X-Idempotency-Cache-Hit: true`"), so reuse the key when retrying the same operation and use a new one for a new operation. X-Trace-Id is optional. For both: "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters." "Its length should be between 12 and 255 characters." The idempotency page also says "We recommend using a **UUID** string as your idempotency key": strip the UUID's hyphens to satisfy both.

type picks the corridor and its required fields (one schema branch per type): bank_ngn needs only bank{account_number, code}; bank_ghs / rwf / sll / ugx / xaf / xof need name + bank{account_number, code, branch}; bank_etb / kes / mwk need name + bank{account_number, code} (mwk: branch optional); bank_eur needs name, phone, email, address + bank{account_number, name, swift_code}; bank_gbp needs name, phone, email, address + bank{account_number, account_type, name, sort_code} (no swift_code); bank_usd needs name, phone, email, address + bank{account_number, code, account_type, routing_number, swift_code}; bank_zar and bank_egp need full KYC. mobile_money_* need name + mobile_money{network, msisdn}; mobile_money_egp also national_identification + address. Names: ASCII letters, 2-50 characters (^(?![ ,.'-]*$)[A-Za-z ,.'-]{2,50}$), so transliterate accented names.

Mobile money: Docs (Mobile Money Transfers): "The `msisdn` field must contain the recipient’s mobile number **starting with the country code**." "For `XAF` and `XOF` transfers, include the country field explicitly in the request."

Codes: bank.code comes from list_banks (the bank's code, not its id); mobile_money.network from list_mobile_networks; bank.branch from list_bank_branches. Docs (General Transfer Flow): "For some countries (e.g., Ghana), you may also need to call the [retrieve bank branches](/v4.0/reference/bank_branches_get) endpoint to get branch codes."
This endpoint only creates bank_* and mobile_money_* recipients. Wallet payouts go through create_orchestrator_transfer; cash pickup and crypto exist in the API but are not covered by these specs.
Store data.id (rcb_… for bank) for create_transfer. Creating the same beneficiary twice returns 270409 RECIPIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS: reuse the existing id (list_transfer_recipients).

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 270409 RECIPIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS, 252400 UNKNOWN_BANK_CODE, 251400 INVALID_ACCOUNT. Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
